_about: The rules every article figure meets before anyone sees it (Krish, 19 Nov 2026, Fri 20 production session: "these dont look visually good enough and they have the wrong brand mark. Are these to go inside, in line, in the Substack article? If so, we don't even need the brand mark."). Read by scripts/pages/figure_check.py, which scripts/pages/render_figure.mjs runs on every figure before it draws it. A new rule is a row here, never a copy in a script. config/failures.json article-figure-typed-mark-and-word-cards.

kinds.inline: A figure that sits inside the Substack article, which already carries the brand: no mark of any kind.
kinds.share-card: A figure made to be shared alone, away from the article (a ruling Krish has not made yet, built to the house rule meanwhile): it may carry the wordmark only as the palette's own image (config/brand-palette.json marks), never typed text.

forms.source-page: the real page, cropped, with its date
forms.scale: bars or areas drawn to the true ratio
forms.comparison: two or more things side by side, measured the same way

article_match._pairs_why: Words that stand together on a stamp (a pill, a flag, a big number) must stand together in the article: "Billed twice" on a pill made the claim firmer than the article's "billed for a main procedure and then again for every part of it" (reader test 2, Fri 20). Longer labels and sub-lines are held only to using the article's own words, so a fair paraphrase of a sentence passes.

em_dash_in_source_pages.ruling: Words inside a real source's screenshot are the source's own words and are exempt from the no-em-dash rule (the default until Krish rules; failure report of 19 Nov, the Tom's Hardware headline). Everything drawn as text on the figure keeps the rule.
